nodes.label: PlanBench-XL Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Interactive benchmark for evaluating LLM agents' long-horizon planning in large-scale, retrieval-mediated tool ecosystems with 327 retail tasks over 1,665 tools.

nodes.label: Typed Tool Library Construction
nodes.rationale: Systematic generation of 1,665 tools from 56 datatypes via LLM-proposed tool functionalities filtered for redundancy and realism; includes noisy tools simulating real-world ecosystem distractors.

nodes.label: Backend Database with Concrete Values
nodes.rationale: Instantiated retail records with non-trivial values that cannot be inferred from common sense; tool responses match input arguments to records and return output datatype values.

nodes.label: Query Generation Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Three-step process: (1) specify task as (initial_datatypes, target_datatypes), (2) compute ground-truth tool-call sequences via state graph reachability, (3) instantiate and verbalize as natural-language query with ground-truth answer.

nodes.label: Bi-directional Tool Retrieval
nodes.rationale: Three retrieval modes: (1) input-conditioned (forward anticipation from available evidence), (2) output-conditioned (backward anticipation from desired outcome), (3) input-output-conditioned (constrained search).

nodes.label: Retrieval-Time Blocking Module
nodes.rationale: Optional perturbation replacing path-critical tools with three failure types: explicit errors, implicit failures (silent wrong values), semantic misleading tools; preserves solvability via alternative paths.

nodes.label: Agent State Definition
nodes.rationale: Latent state (query, discovered_tools, obtained_datatypes) maintained by environment; tracks progress across tool calls but not directly visible to agent.

nodes.label: Evaluation Metrics Suite
nodes.rationale: Seven metrics: accuracy, EGT precision (task-relevant execution), average turns, mean explored datatypes, search-to-call ratio, invalid tool call rate, untrusted input rejection rate.

nodes.label: Frontier LLM Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Tested 10 models: GPT-5.4 (51.90% accuracy), Gemini-3.1-Pro (77.06%), DeepSeek-V4-Flash (63.08%), Llama-3.3-70B (18.96%), Qwen3 variants (0-2.75%); shows massive-tool planning remains challenging.

nodes.label: Trajectory Drift Failure Mode
nodes.rationale: Models make partial progress then drift away from valid solution paths via non-progress tool calls; recovery is rare (3% of failures), indicating weak adaptive re-planning.

nodes.label: Tool Selection Failure Analysis
nodes.rationale: 78% of failed non-progress calls occur despite useful alternatives already retrieved; models over-select recently retrieved tools (74.1%) even when older tools would advance the task.

nodes.label: Silent Failure Vulnerability
nodes.rationale: Implicit failures (silent wrong values) most harmful: 42.2% value reuse vs 0% for explicit errors; agents treat invalid values as grounded evidence, propagating failures downstream.

nodes.label: Model-Specific Termination Policies
nodes.rationale: GPT surrenders (77.3%), DeepSeek/Llama commit hallucinated values (58-81%), Gemini exhausts search (90.8%); patterns stable across settings, indicating hierarchical failure structure.

nodes.label: Blocking Severity Analysis
nodes.rationale: GPT-5.4 accuracy drops from 51.90% (no block) to 11.36% (longest-path-only block); longer recovery paths especially difficult; enforced exploration yields <5% gains.

nodes.label: Exploration-Exploitation Trade-off
nodes.rationale: Mean explored datatypes (EDT) strongly correlated with accuracy (r=0.902), but high search-to-call ratio does not guarantee success; Gemini-3.5-Flash searches 10x more than Gemini-3.1-Pro with lower EDT.

nodes.label: Bi-directional Anticipation Importance
nodes.rationale: Output-conditioned (backward) retrieval frequency strongly correlated with accuracy (r=0.800); low-performing models rely heavily on input-conditioned (forward) retrieval, missing backward reasoning.

nodes.label: LLM Agent Planning in Tool Ecosystems
nodes.rationale: Emerging research area: agents must discover relevant tools from large sets, infer implicit subgoals, and adapt to dynamic environments; retrieval-mediated access introduces partial observability and unreliability.

nodes.label: PlanBench-XL: A Benchmark for Tool-Using Agents
nodes.rationale: Long-horizon tool-use benchmark with realistic conditions: tool retrieval from large spaces, implicit sub-goals, bi-directional exploration, unreliable tools, and scalable generation

nodes.label: Tool-Use
nodes.rationale: Basic requirement for evaluating agents that interact with external environments through APIs, databases, or executable interfaces

nodes.label: Tool Retrieval
nodes.rationale: Agents must retrieve or discover relevant tools from large tool ecosystems (hundreds or thousands of APIs) during problem solving, rather than having full tool set visible

nodes.label: Implicit Sub-goals
nodes.rationale: Complex tasks rarely specify all intermediate steps explicitly; agents must infer missing information and determine which tools bridge current state to final objective

nodes.label: Bi-directional Exploration
nodes.rationale: Effective exploration proceeds forward from available evidence and backward from desired target outcome, combining forward planning from task goals with backward planning from tool affordances

nodes.label: Unreliable Tools
nodes.rationale: Retrieved tools in real systems may be unavailable, stale, misleading, broken, or only partially relevant; robust agents must evaluate feedback and recover from failures

nodes.label: Long-Horizon Tasks
nodes.rationale: Tasks requiring multiple dependent steps (≥25 turns or ≥5 tool invocations); agents must maintain state, plan across interactions, and avoid compounding errors

nodes.label: Scalable Generation
nodes.rationale: Realistic evaluation requires broad coverage over tasks, tools, and environments; scalable construction pipeline enables systematic stress-testing under many configurations

nodes.label: Tool Schema Construction
nodes.rationale: Each tool has input and output datatype sets; multi-input tools (m ∈ 1-5) match real-world scenarios; tool names use alias-based naming to prevent agents from recovering tool graph via canonical names

nodes.label: Tool Description Generation
nodes.rationale: Natural-language explanations of tool functionality generated by M_gen; clarify contextual meaning of returned datatypes and distinguish tools with similar signatures

nodes.label: Noisy Tool Construction
nodes.rationale: Five noisy variants per executable tool (925 total for 185 executable tools); five noise categories test agent ability to reject unreliable tools using descriptions

nodes.label: Deprecated Tool
nodes.rationale: Tool returns unsupported-endpoint error when invoked; appears normal but is unavailable

nodes.label: Condition-Limited Tool
nodes.rationale: Tool has valid signature but only available under special record conditions not satisfied in benchmark instance

nodes.label: Stale Tool
nodes.rationale: Tool returns right type of field but value comes from outdated cache or lagging replica

nodes.label: Unreliable Tool
nodes.rationale: Tool declares intended output field but returns value from related but wrong backend field

nodes.label: Non-Authoritative Value Tool
nodes.rationale: Tool returns preview, default, estimated, or otherwise non-final value instead of final backend truth

nodes.label: Tool Filtering
nodes.rationale: M_fil screens candidate tools using four criteria: deterministic dependency, tool-grounded information access, domain realism, non-trivial information gain

nodes.label: Deterministic Dependency
nodes.rationale: Input datatype set must be sufficient for determining output datatype set; excludes tools with redundant inputs

nodes.label: Tool-Grounded Information Access
nodes.rationale: Tool must retrieve or derive information from external database, not encode pure reasoning shortcut model could perform without environment interaction

nodes.label: Domain Realism
nodes.rationale: Input-output relation must be plausible under retail domain semantics encoded in database and datatype inventory

nodes.label: Non-Trivial Information Gain
nodes.rationale: Output datatype set must contribute genuinely new state information, not merely rename, format, or echo available values

nodes.label: Direct Search Tool
nodes.rationale: Uses valid input identifiers to look up requested fields in hidden backend database; values inaccessible before execution

nodes.label: Action-Like Tool
nodes.rationale: Represents operation and returns values produced by operation (operation ID, confirmation token, created-record identifier); only available after invocation

nodes.label: State Graph
nodes.rationale: Directed graph G_i = (V_i, E_i) where nodes are agent states (sets of obtained datatypes) and edges are valid tool invocations; used for reachability checks and path enumeration

nodes.label: Algorithm 1: Computing Inclusion-Minimal Tool Sets
nodes.rationale: Backward search from target datatype set to enumerate inclusion-minimal tool sets; maintains antichain under set inclusion to avoid redundant solutions

nodes.label: Process-Level Ground Truth
nodes.rationale: Union of all legal execution orders for inclusion-minimal tool sets; serves as reference for process-level evaluation and forms path catalog

nodes.label: Final Answer Ground Truth
nodes.rationale: Constructed by executing one valid ground-truth path; M_gen walks through sequence and invokes tools in order to obtain target datatype values

nodes.label: Answer Evaluation Protocol
nodes.rationale: Normalized containment matching: lowercase, remove markup/quotes, collapse whitespace; prediction correct when normalized gold answer appears as substring of normalized prediction

nodes.label: Retriever
nodes.rationale: Maps agent's natural-language request to canonical datatypes; returns tools satisfying typed constraints; supports three lookup modes (input-conditioned, output-conditioned, input-output-conditioned)

nodes.label: Request Matching Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Encodes query phrase and datatype aliases with lightweight hashing (word tokens, bigrams, trigrams); selects top-1 datatype by cosine-style sparse-vector similarity; caps results at 30 tools

nodes.label: Input-Conditioned Retrieval
nodes.rationale: Agent specifies input datatype set; retriever returns tools whose input datatype set matches requested constraint (unordered set matching)

nodes.label: Output-Conditioned Retrieval
nodes.rationale: Agent specifies output datatype set; retriever returns tools whose output datatype set matches requested constraint (unordered set matching)

nodes.label: Input-Output-Conditioned Retrieval
nodes.rationale: Agent specifies both input and output datatype sets; retriever returns tools whose typed interface satisfies both constraints

nodes.label: Runtime Protocol
nodes.rationale: Enforces datatype constraints during tool execution and final-answer evaluation; prevents tool calls before required inputs available; verifies target datatypes present at evaluation

nodes.label: Datatype Checking
nodes.rationale: Before tool execution, all required input datatypes must be present in internal state; at final-answer evaluation, internal state must contain all target datatypes

nodes.label: Tool Availability
nodes.rationale: Agent may only call tools returned by retriever; callable set accumulated across retrieval rounds

nodes.label: Tool Output Resolution
nodes.rationale: For valid tool call, environment resolves values for output datatype set; each valid call determines unique output-value tuple; reports error if no matching tuple found

nodes.label: Termination Conditions
nodes.rationale: Environment finalizes query when step budget reached or final answer submitted; each model response counts as one step

nodes.label: Accuracy Metric
nodes.rationale: Measures whether agent produces correct final answer after following runtime protocol; answer must match gold answer and target datatype must be reached

nodes.label: Execution-Ground-Truth Precision
nodes.rationale: Measures fraction of successfully executed datatypes that appear in process-level ground-truth datatype set; only counts trusted successful tool outputs

nodes.label: Average Turns Metric
nodes.rationale: Reports average number of interaction turns; each model response counts as one turn including retrieval requests, tool calls, final answers, and invalid actions

nodes.label: Mean Explored Datatype Count
nodes.rationale: Measures how broadly agent explores datatype space; explored datatype closure initialized from input datatypes and expanded by successful executions and retrieved tool implications

nodes.label: Search-to-Call Ratio
nodes.rationale: Compares frequency of tool retrieval against tool execution; larger value indicates more retrieval activity relative to execution

nodes.label: Invalid Tool-Call Ratio
nodes.rationale: Measures fraction of attempted tool calls that violate runtime protocol for structural reasons (parsing failure, unretrieved tool, mismatched arguments, missing inputs)

nodes.label: Untrusted Input Rejection Rate
nodes.rationale: Measures fraction of attempted tool calls rejected because one or more arguments come from noisy-tool outputs (untrusted inputs)

nodes.label: Blocking Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Implemented by replacing selected tools in retrieval results; when agent retrieves blocked tool, environment removes it and returns replacement tool instead

nodes.label: Semantic Misleading Blocking
nodes.rationale: Retrieved tool superficially similar to blocked tool but description/schema reveals different function; if invoked, response consistent with tool's own description; detected after retrieval with medium signal explicitness

nodes.label: Explicit Failure Blocking
nodes.rationale: Retrieved tool appears usable before invocation but calling it returns explicit error/failure message; detected after tool call with high signal explicitness; misaligned with tool description

nodes.label: Implicit Failure Blocking
nodes.rationale: Retrieved tool appears usable and returns value without explicit error but response violates tool's described behavior or task-world consistency; detected after tool call with low signal explicitness; misaligned

nodes.label: GPT-5.2
nodes.rationale: Used as M_gen for data construction and final answer generation; used as M_fil for tool filtering

nodes.label: PlanBench-XL Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Multi-step tool-use planning benchmark designed to evaluate agent exploration, exploitation, and adaptive re-planning in large-scale tool ecosystems under partial observability and dynamic blocking.

nodes.label: Tool Construction via GPT-5.2
nodes.rationale: Additional tools generated by M_gen=GPT-5.2 conditioned on original tool name, description, input/output datatypes to preserve retrieval-facing form while modifying behavior according to blocking type.

nodes.label: Blocking Perturbation Types
nodes.rationale: Three complementary failure modes: explicit failure (tool returns error), implicit failure (tool returns counterfactual/invalid output), semantic misleading (tool supports different function but similar description).

nodes.label: Explicit Failure Block
nodes.rationale: Simulates tools that appear relevant at retrieval time but fail upon invocation (deprecated API, unavailable service, expired auth, schema change). Tests adaptive planning and recovery from visible failures.

nodes.label: Implicit Failure Block
nodes.rationale: Models tool failures where output is syntactically valid but semantically invalid (negative exchange rate, temperature below absolute zero, unrelated information). Tests robustness to silent misinformation.

nodes.label: Semantic Misleading Block
nodes.rationale: Represents retrieval noise where returned tool is semantically close but supports different function (e.g., estimated delivery date vs. pickup date). Tests fine-grained tool understanding under retrieval noise.

nodes.label: Blocked Tool Set Selection
nodes.rationale: Path-based blocking objective: selects which tools to block such that at least one feasible solution path remains, preserving task solvability while requiring recovery through alternative paths.

nodes.label: Feasibility Constraints
nodes.rationale: Main block setting uses target remaining-path count n*=1, tolerance δ=1, minimum remaining-path count n_min=1, requiring n_i(C) ∈ {1,2} to ensure at least one feasible path survives blocking.

nodes.label: Finite Candidate Enumeration
nodes.rationale: Blocked tool candidate selection performed over finite enumerated pool rather than all subsets, with enumeration up to size K_blk and bounded by maximum candidate number limit.

nodes.label: Seeded Tie-Breaking
nodes.rationale: Task-specific seed σ_i = σ_0 + hash(i) ensures reproducible blocked tool set selection across multiple candidates with same deviation from target remaining-path count.

nodes.label: Returned-List Budget under Blocking
nodes.rationale: Per-retrieval cap Λ^cap_ret = 30 maintained across settings. For m selected tools, returned list contains K + 2m primary tools (original minus m, plus 3m blocking replacements), with remaining slots filled by noisy distractors.

nodes.label: Error Mode: Irrecoverable Drift
nodes.rationale: Agent obtains useful intermediate evidence, then takes non-progress step and turns off-path tool value into final answer instead of continuing toward target datatype.

nodes.label: Error Mode: Search Exhaustion
nodes.rationale: After partial progress, agent continues retrieving and calling tools but never grounds target answer, exhausting interaction budget without reaching target datatype.

nodes.label: Error Mode: Format Error
nodes.rationale: Repeated invalid tool calls (e.g., passing default_payment_method_id where payment_method_id required) terminate run before agent can stabilize on valid solution path.

nodes.label: Error Mode: Silent Failure Output Accepted
nodes.rationale: Blocked alternative returns plausible target-typed value (e.g., -2147483648 for payment_intent_id) that agent accepts as grounded evidence, contaminating subsequent trajectory.

nodes.label: Error Mode: Premature Answering
nodes.rationale: Agent follows valid prefix of solution path but answers with semantically adjacent value (e.g., order_status instead of auth_status) instead of continuing toward target datatype.

nodes.label: Error Mode: Unresolved Execution
nodes.rationale: Agent follows correct early prefix and continues executing valid actions but spends too much budget on additional retrieval, never committing to final answer before step limit.

nodes.label: Error Mode: Noisy Response Adoption
nodes.rationale: Agent reaches target datatype but accepts corrupted target-typed value (e.g., 'aaabbbundefined' for account_number) and returns it as final answer.

nodes.label: Retail Domain Context
nodes.rationale: Benchmark instantiated in retail domain with record types: customer accounts, products/variants, draft orders, finalized orders, payment methods/attempts/authorizations, fulfillment requests/shipments/delivery attempts, returns/reviews/refunds.

nodes.label: Retail Business Flow Model
nodes.rationale: Main flow: customer account → draft order → pricing/quote → finalized order. Payment flow: saved method → payment attempt → authorization → completed payment. Fulfillment: order → warehouse request → shipment → delivery attempts. After-sales: return request → review → refund.

nodes.label: Datatype-Grounded Construction
nodes.rationale: Benchmark construction grounded in predefined domain-specific datatypes representing distinct kinds of retail information. Tools generated by pairing different input/output datatype sets, making query distribution diverse at semantic and structural levels.

nodes.label: Simplified Retriever Design
nodes.rationale: Retriever abstracts away real-world complexity (noisy documentation, imperfect ranking, dynamic catalogs) by grounding matching in predefined datatype structure. Enables reproducible evaluation and fine-grained analysis while leaving realistic retriever noise for future extensions.

nodes.label: Task Complexity Control
nodes.rationale: Complexity controlled by underlying state graph rather than surface-level linguistic difficulty. Only tasks requiring at least five distinct tool calls retained, ensuring non-trivial multi-step reasoning and ~25 turns average in default setting.

nodes.label: Exploration-Oriented Metrics
nodes.rationale: Dedicated metrics capture breadth and diversity of intermediate information uncovered by agent, disentangling whether strong performance depends on discovering intermediate information, navigating tool space, or accurately executing over explored tools.

nodes.label: Dynamic Blocking Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Evaluates whether agents adapt when originally useful tools become unavailable or unreliable, reflecting realistic large-scale tool environments where robust agents must detect disruption, revise plans, and recover through alternative paths.

nodes.label: Domain-General Design
nodes.rationale: Core design domain-general: can be adapted to other domains (travel, enterprise workflow, customer support, healthcare, finance, software engineering) by replacing domain-specific datatypes, tools, and backend database while preserving exploration protocol and blocking mechanism.

nodes.label: Implicit Sub-Goal Exploration
nodes.rationale: Agents must infer what information is missing, retrieve relevant tools, and construct valid multi-step solution path. Applies to any task where user provides initial information and desired outcome but leaves intermediate sub-goals and tool-use path implicit.

nodes.label: Future Work: Diversity-Aware Tool Exploration
nodes.rationale: Agents should retrieve tools with explicit diversity objectives: forward from known evidence, backward from desired target, bridge queries connecting known and missing information. Optimizable using exploration-oriented signals like increasing breadth of useful explored datatypes.

nodes.label: Future Work: Failure-Aware Tool Verification
nodes.rationale: Agents need verification phase after suspicious tool calls: check output type validity, semantic plausibility, contradiction with previous evidence, independent confirmation. Especially useful for implicit failure blocks producing counterfactual values.

nodes.label: Future Work: Backtracking-Based Recovery Planning
nodes.rationale: Agents equipped with explicit backtracking and recovery policies: mark unreliable paths, roll back to most recent valid state, search alternative paths from current evidence or final target. Targets longest-path setting requiring recovery through less direct tool chains.

nodes.label: Future Work: Blocker-Aware Training
nodes.rationale: Train agents on trajectories explicitly containing retrieval misses, explicit errors, implicit errors, semantic distractions. Learn recovery behaviors: recognize blocked paths, avoid repeated failed calls, discard suspicious observations, search alternatives. Reinforcement learning natural fit with executable feedback.

nodes.label: Enforced-Exploration Analysis
nodes.rationale: When agent attempts incorrect final answer, insert user message asking continued exploration. Results show additional interaction brings <5% gains, suggesting main bottleneck is adaptive re-planning under partial observability, not simple search over known state space.

nodes.label: Evaluation Fairness Design
nodes.rationale: Same blocking configuration applied to every model within each setting. Blocked tools pre-computed and fixed across all models, ensuring identical solution space changes and enabling attribution of performance differences to model ability rather than blocking conditions.

nodes.label: Single-Step Tool Retrieval Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Sanity check: for each tool τ, create one-step task with D_in(τ) as initial datatypes and D_out(τ) as target. Tests whether retriever and runtime provide reliable access to correct tools, showing lower multi-step performance due to planning/state-tracking rather than retriever failure.

nodes.label: Bootstrap Confidence Intervals
nodes.rationale: Non-parametric bootstrap resampling 10,000 times over N=327 evaluated queries to estimate 95% confidence intervals. Average radius 2.94 percentage points for Accuracy, suggesting main trends unlikely artifacts of test-set sampling noise.

nodes.label: Seed Robustness Verification
nodes.rationale: Reran blocked evaluation with seeds 1000, 2000, 3000 showing <3% variation across seeds, indicating block setting conclusions not sensitive to particular seeded blocker configuration.

nodes.label: Human Annotation Quality Study
nodes.rationale: Five annotators evaluated 50 tools and 25 datatypes on 1-5 Likert scale for reasonableness/realism. Tools averaged 4.32, datatypes 4.56, indicating high quality and alignment with realistic retail-domain scenarios.

nodes.label: Inference Prompt System
nodes.rationale: System prompt instructs agent to solve queries via tool planning under 100-step budget. Provides domain context, business flow overview, planning intuition, action usage rules, tool selection guidance, correctness validation, and execution strategy.

nodes.label: Tool Schema Structure
nodes.rationale: Agent-visible schema includes function name, description, parameters, strictness constraints. Internal metadata includes input/output datatypes used for retrieval, dependency validation, progress-call annotation, evaluation. Distinction important for error analysis.

nodes.label: Representative Retail Task Example
nodes.rationale: retail_task_0001: from delivery_attempt_id, find account_number through 8-step path spanning fulfillment, order, return, and payment subflows. Demonstrates why benchmark is not single-hop lookup and why failures can occur at multiple points.
